transcript:
Header:
- Date: 2026-03-03
- Time: 14:00 UTC
- Duration: ~58 minutes
- Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Leah Wong (Redwood SE), Jasper Chen (Redwood CSM), Dr. Emily Hart (Nimbus Data Science), Marcus Lee (Nimbus Platform), Priya Nair (Nimbus Security)

Summary:
- Weekly POC sync focused on rollout/go-live plan: canary, A/B options, cutover steps, monitoring and runbooks.
- Customer wants minimal blast radius, clear rollback, and compliance signoff before prod traffic.
- Action items assigned for canary schedule, runbook, capacity numbers, and security confirmations.

Topics:
- Canary vs. A/B canary design, traffic percentages and duration
- Monitoring signals: latency p95/p99, error rates, token cost, model quality regressions
- Runbooks: automated rollback, throttles, fallback model variants, alerting channels
- Cutover timing: weekend vs weekday, stakeholder on-call windows
- Compliance: SOC2, KMS, audit logs, data residency

Transcript:
[00:00] Samir: hey everyone thanks for joining on time, appreciate it. quick agenda: finish canary plan, confirm monitoring, runbook owners, and cutover timing. anyone need to add?
[00:12] Dr. Emily: no that's right. we've been looking at the week-to-week evals, and the quality looks stable, but we want to make sure the canary captures edge-case prompts from clinical notes.
[00:25] Leah: got it. we've added the clinical prompt set in the evaluation harness. small caveat, the KV cache patterns shift token usage a bit, so cost per session fluctuates during longer notes.
[00:37] Marcus: yeah that was one thing, when we ramped up a small load last week we saw p95 spike at around 600ms which is fine but p99 popped a few times. want to confirm acceptable SLOs.
[00:49] Priya: from security side we need KMS integration verified and audit logs retained for 90 days, also need confirmation on encryption at rest for cached prompts.
[01:02] Samir: thanks, all noted. for SLOs Leah suggested 300ms p95 for the dedicated model path and fallback to a slightly smaller quantized variant if latency breaks. Leah?
[01:15] Leah: right, our recommended canary is layered: 1) start 1% traffic for 24 hours, monitor key metrics, 2) 5% for 12 hours, 3) 20% for 6 hours then full if green. fallback rules are automated: >2% error rate for 10 minutes triggers immediate shift to fallback model; >300ms p99 for 5 minutes triggers throttling. these numbers are tunable.
[01:40] Dr. Emily: 1% seems small, will that surface real quality issues? clinical prompts are rare.
[01:48] Leah: good point—if you want we can do targeted routing for specific clinical-similar user IDs so the small percentage still hits edge cases. it's like A/B but with rule-based targeting.
[02:03] Marcus: that helps. for capacity planning we need expected QPS peak and burst patterns. we're still finalizing, but want Redwood to autoscale quickly. do you have warmup guidance?
[02:15] Samir: yes, we'll provide an autoscale profile. for dedicated we've set up minimal warm pool to avoid cold starts and maintain low latency. warmup takes ~30s for new model shards but KV cache warms slower—so we recommend gradual ramp for large shifts.
[02:34] Priya: also need to know where logs are stored. do you push to our S3, or do you keep them in Redwood console?
[02:41] Jasper: current plan is logs and traces go to your S3 via a secure endpoint; audit logs also mirrored to your Splunk/Datadog if you want. permissioned via a customer-managed KMS key.
[02:52] Priya: okay please send the exact bucket naming and ARN.
[02:56] Samir: will do.
[03:00] (30s break while doc link is pasted)
[03:34] Leah: turning to rollback playbook. main scenarios: model regression, runtime errors (OOMs), and infra capacity issues. for model regression we have evaluation hooks that check quality on a small labeled set; if regression detected beyond threshold we auto-flag and can auto-roll back to previous pinned model.
[03:55] Dr. Emily: thresholds? what's reasonable? 5% drop in exact-match or 1% drop in our composite score?
[04:02] Leah: typically 1-2% on composite for critical pipelines. we can tune per your clinical prompts.
[04:10] Marcus: about auto rollback—what about transient flakiness? we worry about flip-flopping.
[04:16] Leah: good question. we require sustained signal (e.g., sustained for 10min with >x samples) and a human approve window for re-deploy. auto rollback can be set to require manual confirmation depending on your preference.
[04:30] Samir: we'll default to automatic rollback for infra failures (OOMs, >=5% error) and manual for quality regressions unless you opt-in.
[04:40] Dr. Emily: manual for quality please. we want to triage outputs first.
[04:44] Samir: noted.
[05:00] Marcus: quick note on canary timing—do we prefer weekend to reduce user impact? our ops says weekdays are bad for some teams.
[05:08] Priya: security prefers a weekday because the on-call person is different over the weekend and we may not have all signoffs.
[05:15] Dr. Emily: how long to full roll? multi-day?
[05:20] Leah: with the staged plan it's typically 48 hours for full ramp if green, but you can compress if you want. recommended min observation windows between stages.
[05:32] Samir: propose this schedule: start Friday 00:00 UTC with 1% targeted traffic (clinical IDs included), monitor through Friday business hours, increase Monday morning to 5% then afternoon to 20, then 100 late Monday if green. That gives weekend buffer and Monday coverage.
[05:50] Marcus: sounds okay, need to confirm with on-call.
[05:54] Priya: also want to ensure pagers for certain alerts only go to a small ops list first. we shouldn't Page an entire SRE team for token cost spikes.
[06:03] Jasper: we'll set up alert routing: critical infra -> SRE on-call; model quality degradation -> triage channel to Data Science + AE/SE; cost anomalies -> billing list and your cost-owner.
[06:20] Samir: next, monitoring signals. Leah, can you list the dashboard panels we'll watch?
[06:27] Leah: yes: 1) latency p50/p95/p99, 2) request error rate (4xx/5xx), 3) model quality regression score on sentinel prompts, 4) token consumption and cost per minute, 5) KV cache hit ratio, 6) GPU utilization, 7) queue depth and batch sizes. We'll also have a synthesized health score for the canary that aggregates these.
[06:49] Dr. Emily: the sentinel prompts need to include clinical negation cases—we'll share a small labeled set.
[06:55] Samir: please share that list by Thursday.
[06:58] Dr. Emily: okay.
[07:02] Marcus: on the fallback model: what's the quality delta between main and fallback?
[07:07] Leah: fallback is a smaller quantized variant, quality loss is typically small for general queries but for clinical edge cases it can be 2-5% in our local metrics; hence targeted routing for those prompts is important.
[07:22] Dr. Emily: we might want a second canary that runs the fallback variant in parallel for an A/B sanity check.
[07:29] Leah: doable. that would be an A/B with mirrored traffic; we can report back results in the second week.
[07:35] Samir: ok action item—Leah propose A/B config and expected metrics for week 2.
[07:40] Leah: noted.
[07:43] Marcus: what's the cutover contractually—do we need a signed acceptance?
[07:48] Samir: typical process: we run the canary and when the canary health score is green for the agreed observation window (we'll state this in the SOW), Nimbus signs the acceptance and we flip traffic. we can align with your procurement timeline.
[08:00] Priya: procurement will need a sync with legal. also share SOC2 attestation and KMS docs.
[08:07] Samir: I'll attach the SOC2 report and the KMS integration doc after the call.
[08:12] Dr. Emily: about runbooks—we want explicit steps for these scenarios: degrade quality, spike latency, high cost, and full outage. can you include play-by-play?
[08:23] Leah: yes, runbook will include checklists: initial triage steps, commands to flip traffic, how to pin model versions, and who to call. we'll also include CLI commands for emergency rollback.
[08:34] Jasper: plus contact tree with phone numbers and escalation rules.
[08:38] Marcus: test drill—can we do a dry-run of a rollback next week in staging?
[08:44] Leah: absolutely, we can schedule a fire-drill. recommend doing it during mid-week staging window so it's low risk.
[08:52] Samir: propose we do the drill Wednesday 2026-03-11. Marcus/Priya can you confirm?
[08:57] Marcus: tentatively yes, I'll confirm after I sync with ops.
[09:01] Priya: I'll check security calendar.
[09:04] Dr. Emily: one more thing—cost controls. we need hard budget alerts and soft throttles.
[09:10] Leah: we support pre-commit budget caps and soft throttles that start rejecting or queueing non-critical requests if we near budget. also token-level budgeting per route.
[09:22] Marcus: how does that interact with the canary? don't want budget throttle to interfere with canary traffic.
[09:27] Leah: we can exclude canary routes from throttles or set higher budget for them.
[09:31] Samir: ok we'll make canary exempt.
[09:34] (brief crosstalk)
[09:50] Jasper: summary of decisions so far: staged canary with targeted clinical routing, manual rollback for quality regressions, automatic for infra, runbook + escalate channels, fire-drill planned, SOC2/KMS docs to be sent.
[10:05] Dr. Emily: sounds good. can we get a written schedule and runbook by end of week?
[10:12] Samir: yes. we'll send a combined doc and calendar invites.
[10:16] Leah: action items noted—I'll draft the runbook and A/B config, Samir will send canary schedule, Jasper will set alert routing, Marcus/Priya to confirm calendars and capacity.
[10:28] Priya: quick Q on audit logs retention: can we get 1 year if needed? our compliance team sometimes requires 12 months.
[10:36] Samir: retention is configurable; default 90 days but we can extend to 12 months for an enterprise add-on. I'll include pricing implications.
[10:48] Marcus: pricing note—if we keep a larger warm pool this will add to monthly cost. want a breakdown before we finalize.
[10:55] Samir: will include a cost delta doc.
[11:02] (wrap up)
[11:10] Samir: recap of next steps and owners, will share docs and schedule by Friday. thanks everyone.
[11:16] Dr. Emily: thanks all.
[11:20] (call ends)
